newsitem.title: UK: UK rates at 6.75 pct by end-97, Lloyds says.
newsitem.headline: UK rates at 6.75 pct by end-97, Lloyds says.

text.p: UK interest rates may need to rise by one percentage point by the end of 1997 if the British government wants to keep inflation under control, Lloyds-TSB Group said on Monday.
Base rates are expected to end next year at 6.75 percent as consumer spending booms over the next 12 months, said Patrick Foley, Lloyds Bank's chief economic adviser.
He said economic growth could reach 3.75 percent in 1997 as consumer spending accelerates further, fuelled by higher incomes and a sustained housing market recovery.
"Although the housing market is still relatively weak...it appears to be more sustainable than the false starts we have seen in the last three years," Foley said.
"But given the experience of the 1980s, any signs of the house market recovery turning into a boom are likely to prompt a rapid interest rate response from the government."

Foley said a rate rise prior to elections, which must be held by May 1997, was unlikely. As a result, he forecast inflation would push up to around 3.5 percent before falling back, providing the government does tighten monetary policy.
Underlying inflation, excluding mortgage interest payments, edged up to 2.9 percent year-on-year in September.
Foley did not expect significant net tax cuts in the November budget because the economy is growing too strongly to warrant them and public finances are not in sufficiently good shape.
